closure_feasibility.finding: The existing rbo test target depends on ut/common, which already links query SDK. The current Q28 direct adapter selects that production closure. A separate anonymous timing adapter can use those symbols without adding production dependencies; this remains source feasibility, not a link-success claim.
closure_feasibility.separation: Keep any future timing adapter and its evidence separately fingerprinted. Do not replace the existing 26-case scheduler generator/admission record.

conclusion: A small anonymous adapter can obtain actual server-reported compilation wall time, CPU time and cache status through the existing query SDK in the RBO test closure, independently of new-RBO plan JSON. Production edits are unnecessary for this data path. Native linking/execution remains unverified, and these counters are neither pure RBO time nor complete request latency.
coordination: Sibling remaining_correctness_review owns the Q28 semantic/profile generator and final-plan observer. This report only covers compilation-statistics APIs and measurement limits.

data_path.observation: Reply writes uncached compilation elapsed wall time and the CompileCpuTime accumulator.
SaveAndCheckCompileResult assigns compile response statistics to query state.
Pinned-source FillSystemViewQueryStats copies compilation duration/CPU/cache when CompileResult exists, independently from total query/worker CPU.
TKqpQueryStats::ToProto serializes the dedicated Compilation message.
The dedicated protobuf is attached independently of SerializeAnalyzePlan.
FillQueryStats maps the dedicated compilation fields into Ydb.TableStats.QueryStats. Its total CPU field separately includes execution, worker and compilation CPU.
Final generic-query response invokes FillQueryStats independently of plan JSON.
SDK constructs TExecStats from exec_stats; buffered execution retains the latest final stats at line190.

direct_request_reference: ydb/public/sdk/cpp/src/client/query/client.cpp:981: TSession::ExecuteQuery forwards the request and applies session-status interception; use this direct API rather than RetryQuery.

exact_api_route.purpose: Create one bounded actual server; finish startup and setup before the target request.
Submit sibling-generated SQL held only in RAM; use one request, not a retry wrapper.
Collect dedicated compilation statistics with minimal execution-statistics detail; keep settings identical across revisions.
Require successful final result, present stats and present optional compilation message.
Export exactly the cache boolean and two unsigned microsecond counters; missing statistics are not zero samples.

kqprun_output_limit.finding: stats-mode controls collection, but TQueryMeta retains AST, plan and total query duration. script-plan-file and script-statistics expose plan-derived data, not the separate compilation submessage. No existing CLI switch found that exports that submessage. full-proto result format is result-set output, not the complete query response.
invalid_substitutes: in-progress CPU usage derived from plan JSON

metric_limits: The counters cover compiler accounting across phases, not only RBO or the changed rules. They cannot identify a dominant optimizer stage.

Wall time begins at StartCompilation (kqp_compile_actor.cpp:278) and ends at Reply. It includes waits/metadata work within that interval but excludes runner startup, client transport and compile-service queue time before the interval.

With EnableAstCache, the service can run a separate PARSE/cache lookup before COMPILE (kqp_compile_service.cpp:615). Those earlier phases are not necessarily included. Query state assigns one CompileStats response rather than proving aggregate timing across split statements or retries; restrict samples to one generated read-only statement and reject failures/retries.

CPU is the existing CompileCpuTime accumulator, scoped at StartCompilationWithSettings (line320) and continuation handling (line587). It is not exhaustive process CPU: initial Continue at316 and final response processing are outside those scopes. Label it server-reported compilation CPU, not complete optimizer CPU.
Public CompilationStats has no per-stage fields or UsedNewRbo flag. Enforce new RBO enabled, fallback disabled, and the existing configuration/plan proof separately.

Cache-hit responses set FromCache=true with default timing counters (kqp_compile_service.cpp:1039). Zero alone cannot distinguish missing, cached or very short work; require optional-message presence and explicit cache state and treat zero timings as uninformative for a speed claim.

Fresh-runner measurements include cold metadata effects inside compilation. Warm-metadata measurements need a separately validated cache invalidation route; this report does not assume cache size0 or new-session cache bypass.
Explain and Full/Profile collect extra diagnostics. Samples with different modes cannot be compared as the same workload. Explain alone proves no result semantics.
The anonymous adapter has not been implemented, linked or executed. Actual successful compilation-stat return and cache controls still need native verification. No production speedup is claimed.

Using one SELECT and avoiding RetryQuery prevents an explicit SDK retry loop, but the public compilation submessage does not prove absence of internal recompile attempts; do not claim it aggregates every attempt without additional native evidence.
narrow_measurement_route: Consume the sibling Q28 case/schema/fixture generator through inherited memfds or RAM; do not create another semantic generator or persist rendered SQL.
Use one fresh isolated runner and one target compilation per process/sample. Complete startup, schema, fixtures and session creation first; no process stopwatch is used as compilation evidence.

Prefer normal Execute with Basic stats for a small read-only target. Pass returned rows to the existing independent semantic oracle separately; only the compilation submessage supplies timing. If Full is needed to match the sibling structural run, keep that mode identical across both revisions and label it.

Explain with Basic stats is a non-executing alternative: Explain always reports stats at rpc_execute_query.cpp:151, while Basic explicitly enables session stats collection. Explain also requests AST/diagnostics, so label its samples separately and retain independent execution semantics.

Require IsFromCache=false for every cold compilation sample. Generic query RPC unconditionally requests keep_in_cache=true at rpc_execute_query.cpp:303, and NQuery settings offer no Table-client KeepInQueryCache equivalent. Fresh sessions, changed comments and assumed cache-size-zero behavior are not valid cache-bypass proofs.
A disposable repeated query can provide a cache-hit negative control if the statement is cacheable. Require the actual true flag; missing hits stay pending and never count as cheaper compilation.

Match query/schema/fixture/config/execution-mode hashes across exact baseline and fixed revisions, and retain production closure/executable provenance. Run one native server at a time under existing memory/process-group guards and the serial verification slot; never overlap the active build.

Emit only case/repetition/phase/revision, provenance/workload hashes, stats presence, cache flag, compilation duration_us/cpu_time_us, success and independent semantic flags. Do not serialize stats ToString(), AST/plan/meta, generated SQL or raw issues.

Keep server/compiler diagnostics in anonymous bounded memory or discarded by the existing guard; TKikimrSettings::SetLogCapture and TCapturedLog exist at kqp_ut_common.h:148 and:49. Never print captured logs or unsanitized issue messages. Capture structured measurements separately from startup output.

Use repeated paired uncached measurements to describe overall server compilation-accounting trends and regressions. Retain direct scheduler work counters and sibling final-plan semantics separately. This report proposes no automatic quality acceptance or performance threshold.
